turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Patient: I’ve been dealing with progressively worsening generalized fatigue for about two months, and my skin looks paler than usual. I’ve also noticed multiple tiny red, non-blanching spots on my extremities, and I get mild shortness of breath when I exert.
[ASK] Have you had episodes of severe chest pain/shortness of breath with a stress-related trigger and heart imaging showing Takotsubo (broken-heart) pattern?

“No, I haven’t had any severe chest pain or sudden stress-triggered episodes, and I don’t know of any heart imaging that ever showed a broken-heart pattern—my shortness of breath is only mild with exertion.”
[ASK] Have you developed new skin lesions that are painful and ulcerate (e.g., rapidly worsening painful ulcers or skin breakdown)?
Patient: No, I haven’t had painful lesions or ulcers—just multiple tiny red, non-blanching spots on my extremities that I’ve noticed over time. I don’t have any rapid skin breakdown.
[ASK] Have you had **unexplained bleeding or easy bruising** (e.g., frequent nose/gum bleeding, blood in urine/stool, or unusually heavy bleeding)?
“Doctor, I haven’t noticed unusual bleeding or easy bruising—no frequent nose or gum bleeding, no blood in my urine or stool, and my bruising hasn’t seemed heavier than normal.”
[ASK] Do you have **visible rectal bleeding with pain/itching consistent with hemorrhoids** (e.g., bright red blood on toilet paper or pain during bowel movements)?

“No— I haven’t seen any bright red rectal bleeding, and I haven’t had pain or itching with bowel movements. My main issue has been the worsening fatigue, paler skin, and those tiny non-blanching red spots on my extremities.”

[ASK] Does the patient have **bleeding due to a clotting factor deficiency** (e.g., frequent nose/gum bleeding, easy bruising, prolonged bleeding after minor cuts) rather than symptoms of cancer or sudden abdominal ischemia?

“No, I haven’t had frequent nose or gum bleeding, prolonged bleeding after minor cuts, or unusually easy bruising—I mostly just feel progressively more fatigued, look paler, and I’ve noticed those tiny red non-blanching spots on my extremities.”
[ASK] Do you have **sudden severe abdominal pain** (especially with nausea/vomiting) that started **within the last 24 hours**?

“No, I don’t have sudden severe abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting—my symptoms have been steadily worsening over about two months, mainly fatigue, paler skin, and those tiny non-blanching red spots on my extremities.”
